start_here: Say to your AI: "Export my Arc browser's YouTube login from Profile 1 to ~/private/cookies.txt so yt-dlp can download as me." It reads the tool row, asks you before touching your login, and has you run the one command in your own Terminal.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: it reads one browser profile's cookie database and writes a cookies.txt file.
instructions: 1. Check you are signed in to YouTube in the browser profile you will name (browser arc, brave, chrome, chromium, edge or vivaldi; profile Default, Profile 1 ...).
2. Install the package once: python3 -m pip install -U cryptography. Say "Export my browser's YouTube login for yt-dlp"; your AI reads the row with tools:list.
3. Run the command it gives you in your own Terminal and choose Always Allow when macOS asks for the browser's Safe Storage key.

4. Read the last line: {"result": {out, cookies, domains, browser, profile}} names the file and its count, {"error": ...} says what to change. Then pass the file to yt-dlp with --cookies. The file is your login: keep it private and never share or commit it.

worked_examples.title: Export YouTube and Google cookies from Arc Profile 1
worked_examples.ask: Give yt-dlp my Arc browser's YouTube login.
worked_examples.given: From tools/export-browser-login-cookies-for-yt-dlp/test/test_export_cookies.py (a made-up profile holding 3 youtube.com and google.com cookies and 1 example.org cookie) and do-work/export_cookies.py. After tools:list the AI gives you: python3 -I tools/export-browser-login-cookies-for-yt-dlp/do-work/export_cookies.py --browser arc --profile "Profile 1" --out ~/private/cookies.txt. Your profile is assumed to hold 3 youtube.com and google.com cookies.
worked_examples.hands_back: The last line printed is {"result": {"out": "~/private/cookies.txt", "cookies": 3, "domains": ["youtube.com", "google.com"], "browser": "arc", "profile": "Profile 1"}}. cookies.txt starts with the line # Netscape HTTP Cookie File, then one tab-separated line per cookie (e.g. .youtube.com, TRUE, /, TRUE, the expiry, TOKA, its decrypted value), and is readable by its owner only (mode 600); the example.org cookie is not written.
